headline: [Deadly Strike!] Drone Attack on Kuwait Kills [2 Italian Technicians]
sub: Kuwait blames Iran; Iran denies role
caption:
⚠️ Deadly Strike! Drone Attack on Kuwait Kills 2 Italian Technicians

Two Italian technicians were killed on Thursday when drones hit military sites in Kuwait, including an air-defence station where they were working. Kuwait's defence ministry called it an Iranian attack. Iran has denied any role.

🔹 Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said the two men worked for the defence company Rheinmetall Italia. Two other people were injured: a Pakistani national and a Kuwaiti army captain.
🔹 Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told Kuwait and Italy that Iran had "no role or involvement whatsoever" and offered to help find the origin of the attack.
🔹 Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said her thoughts were with all those affected and their families.

💬 What should be done to keep workers and civilians safe in the Gulf? 👇

Sources: Reuters, AP, CNN

#GlobalEye #Kuwait #Italy #Iran #MiddleEast
photo_needed: Kuwait City skyline, or Kuwaiti air-defence / military site, or Italian FM Antonio Tajani speaking (face clearly visible). A big, clear, landscape photo works best.

headline: [Refinery Hit!] Strike on Saudi [Jazan Refinery] Kills One Worker
sub: Coalition blames Houthis; operations briefly halted
caption:
🛢️ Refinery Hit! Strike on Saudi Jazan Refinery Kills One Worker

An aerial projectile hit the Jazan oil refinery on Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coast on Thursday, killing one worker and injuring several others, Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry said. The worker who died was from Nepal.

🔹 The strike started a fire and briefly stopped some operations. The refinery, near the border with Yemen, is built to process up to 400,000 barrels of crude oil a day.
🔹 The Saudi-led coalition said Yemen's Houthis carried out the attack, and that it destroyed the missile launcher used, in Hodeidah. There was no immediate statement from the Houthis.
🔹 Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki warned that attacks on civilians and civilian sites "would be met with a firm military response".

💬 Will attacks on oil sites push up fuel prices where you live? 👇

Sources: Reuters, Al Jazeera, CNN

#GlobalEye #SaudiArabia #Jazan #Houthis #Yemen #Oil
photo_needed: The Saudi Aramco Jazan refinery (any recent photo, or with smoke/fire from 26 Nov), or an oil refinery in Saudi Arabia. A big, clear, landscape photo works best.

headline: [Big Claim!] Ukraine Says North Korea Paused [Missile Deliveries] to Russia
sub: Kyiv links it to row over South Korea
caption:
🚀 Big Claim! Ukraine Says North Korea Paused Missile Deliveries to Russia

Ukraine's military intelligence agency (GUR) said on Thursday that North Korea has temporarily stopped sending ballistic missiles and artillery shells to Russia. Reuters said it could not independently verify the report. There was no immediate comment from Russia or North Korea.

🔹 GUR said the pause covers KN-23 ballistic missiles and artillery shells, and also Russian military flights over North Korea. It said North Korean Foreign Minister Choe Son Hui announced the freeze last month.
🔹 GUR linked the move to friction over Russia's contacts with South Korea. It said North Korea is also holding back on a Russian request to raise its troops in Russia from about 8,500 to 50,000.
🔹 GUR said North Korean units are still serving in Russia's Kursk region.

💬 Do you think this report will change anything in the war in Ukraine? 👇

Sources: Reuters, Al Jazeera, Fox News

#GlobalEye #NorthKorea #Russia #Ukraine #KimJongUn

headline: [Peace Push!] Trump Asks Putin to Pull Back [Military Aggression] in Europe
sub: Trump calls Ukraine war a "complete bloodbath"
caption:
🕊️ Peace Push! Trump Asks Putin to Pull Back Military Aggression in Europe

US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that he asked Russian President Vladimir Putin to "pull back all military aggression against territories throughout Europe". He wrote on Truth Social that he raised this during their talks in China last week, "in the hopes that a deal can be made between Russia and Ukraine, and made quickly."

🔹 Trump said a deal is "a strong possibility" and called the war "a complete bloodbath", saying thousands of people are killed every month.
🔹 Speaking to reporters at Mar-a-Lago in Florida, Trump said: "The biggest problem to that settlement is the fact that you have two leaders that really hate each other."
🔹 Trump said he would like Putin to attend the G20 summit in Florida on December 14-15. The Kremlin said no decision has been made on that.

💬 Do you think a Russia-Ukraine peace deal is close? 👇

Sources: Reuters, AFP, RFE/RL

#GlobalEye #Trump #Putin #Russia #Ukraine #PeaceTalks
photo_needed: Donald Trump, face clearly visible (a photo of Trump with Vladimir Putin, e.g. from their meeting in China last week, also works). A big, clear, landscape photo works best.

headline: [Hung Parliament!] New Zealand Election Final Count Leaves Luxon [One Seat Short]
sub: Small Opportunity party holds the balance
caption:
🗳️ Hung Parliament! New Zealand Election Final Count Leaves Luxon One Seat Short

The final count of New Zealand's 7 November election, released on Friday, left no group with a majority. Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's right-wing bloc won 65 of the 130 seats, one seat short of the number needed to govern alone.

🔹 Luxon's National Party lost two seats when special votes were counted. The left-wing bloc led by Labour's Chris Hipkins has 58 seats.
🔹 The centrist Opportunity party, led by Qiulae Wong, won 7 seats and now holds the balance of power.
🔹 Wong has said she will first negotiate with the party that has the most seats. Luxon's bloc needs Opportunity's support to form a government.

💬 Should small parties get to decide who runs a country? 👇

Sources: AP, Reuters

#GlobalEye #NewZealand #NZElection #Luxon #Politics
photo_needed: New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon, face clearly visible (or New Zealand's Parliament building, the 'Beehive', in Wellington). A big, clear, landscape photo works best.

headline: [Pact Sealed!] Turkey Ratifies Defence Pact With [Pakistan and Saudi Arabia]
sub: Three-nation defence talks begin in Islamabad
caption:
🤝 Pact Sealed! Turkey Ratifies Defence Pact With Pakistan and Saudi Arabia

Turkey has completed its approval of the Mecca joint defence agreement with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia. President Recep Tayyip Erdogan signed off on the pact, and it was published in Turkey's Official Gazette on Friday. Turkey's parliament approved it earlier this month.

🔹 The pact treats an attack on any one of the three countries as an attack on all of them.
🔹 It was signed in Mecca in August by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, President Erdogan and Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. Members can only leave after 10 years.
🔹 Senior defence and foreign affairs officials from the three countries are meeting in Islamabad from Friday. AP reports that Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia are on the agenda.

💬 Will this pact make the region safer? 👇

Sources: AP, Reuters

#GlobalEye #Pakistan #Turkey #SaudiArabia #DefencePact #Erdogan
photo_needed: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif (e.g. the Mecca signing in August), or Erdogan alone, faces clearly visible. A big, clear, landscape photo works best.
